edges.label: author of the notes at the centre of the custody claim
edges.note: The memo records Vice Adm. Thomas Wilson being refused access to a program holding a recovered craft on the ground that it sat with a private aerospace contractor and he had no need to know. Davis has never authenticated it; Wilson has denied the meeting.

edges.label: The Wilson notes place Wilson's 1997 inquiry immediately after exposure to Greer's Washington briefings
edges.note: The Disclosure Project briefed members of Congress and officials in Washington in April 1997; the notes record Wilson beginning his search for the programme in the same period.

b.label: AARO Report on the Historical Record of U.S. Government Involvement with UAP, Volume I

edges.label: AARO's 2024 review does not mention the Wilson-Davis notes or Admiral Wilson
edges.note: The most specific custody allegation in the modern record, whose author and subject are both alive and identifiable, is absent from the government's historical review.

edges.label: The 2002 notes and the 2023 sworn testimony describe the same access-denial mechanism
edges.note: Both describe an appropriately cleared official being refused a read-on by programme security officers and contractor gatekeepers on need-to-know grounds. Twenty-one years apart, two officials describe the same wall.

edges.label: The meeting is reported to have taken place at an EG&G facility in Las Vegas
edges.note: EG&G held the Groom Lake support and personnel-transport contracts; the reported venue matters because it places the conversation inside the contractor perimeter it describes.

edges.label: Wilson denies the meeting and the substance attributed to him
edges.note: Wilson's denial is recorded as a primary artefact. It is irreconcilable with Davis's confirmation of authorship, and no agency has attempted to resolve it.
